term_types.name: Consensus network topology
term_types.question: How are nodes arranged and which nodes participate in maintaining consensus?
term_types.description: Classifies blockchain systems by how network nodes are organised, distinguishing equal peer participation from split roles and central control.

values.definition: All nodes are equivalent peers in a P2P network, each able to validate and propagate transactions.
Nodes are split into tracking and validating roles, often in consortium blockchains.
A central authority operates the nodes and controls validation, with a single point of control.

term_types.name: Block-adding access restriction
term_types.question: Who is permitted to add blocks to the ledger?
term_types.description: Distinguishes systems where block-adding is restricted to a defined signer set from those open to anyone.

values.definition: Anyone can participate in adding blocks without restriction to a defined set of signers.
Block-adding is restricted to a defined set of signers chosen by the operator.

term_types.name: Ledger read, write and consensus governance model
term_types.question: Who has read access, write access, and the right to manage consensus on the ledger?
term_types.description: Classifies ledgers by which parties hold read, write and consensus-management rights, distinguishing open public models from permissioned and private ones.

values.definition: Open read, write and consensus rights for all participants.
Open read, but write or consensus rights restricted to approved participants.
All rights granted and controlled by a central organisation.

term_types.name: Consensus mechanism
term_types.question: What rule is used to agree which transactions are recorded and validated?
term_types.description: Classifies the method by which the network reaches agreement on the ledger state.

values.definition: Validators compete through computational work to add blocks.
Validators are selected in proportion to tokens locked as collateral, with randomised or coin-age selection rules.
Stakeholders elect forgers who produce blocks and are penalised for misbehaviour.
Block creation is restricted to pre-selected, identified trusted signers.
Block production depends on committed storage or disk space capacity.
Validation rights are obtained by destroying tokens at unspendable addresses.
Deterministic agreement via Lamport-style BFT voting among known validators, as in federated systems.
Combines two or more base mechanisms, such as PoB with PoS or PoW, often with checkpoints.

term_types.name: Consensus fault tolerance threshold
term_types.question: What proportion of corrupted or malicious participants can the consensus tolerate before failing?
term_types.description: Classifies consensus mechanisms by the adversarial share they withstand, such as the one-third BFT bound or the 25 percent coordinated-attack threshold of proof-of-work.

values.definition: Tolerates corruption of up to one third of nodes, as in BFT mechanisms.
Coordinated attack threshold of about 25 percent of computational or validation power, as in proof-of-work.
Security depends on the proportion of stake controlled by honest parties rather than a fixed node fraction.

term_types.name: Network energy intensity
term_types.question: How energy-intensive is the network's consensus process?
term_types.description: Classifies networks by their energy consumption relative to other systems.

values.definition: Consensus consumes energy at a level comparable to proof-of-work systems such as Bitcoin.
Consensus consumes substantially less energy, as in proof-of-stake systems.

term_types.name: Transaction finality type
term_types.question: Is transaction finality reached with certainty at a fixed point or only probabilistically?
term_types.description: Classifies whether transaction confirmation is guaranteed deterministically or accumulates probabilistically.

values.definition: A transaction is final once a defined confirmation point is reached with certainty.
Finality is probabilistic and grows as further blocks are added.

term_types.name: Network message propagation scope
term_types.question: Is consensus reached locally before propagation, or are messages gossiped globally to random peers?
term_types.description: Classifies how transactions and consensus messages spread across the network, locally within neighbourhoods or globally across peers.

values.definition: Consensus is reached within a local neighbourhood before propagation, as in federated consensus.
Messages propagate to randomly selected peers in an unstructured topology, as in Bitcoin and Ethereum.

term_types.name: Message delivery timing model
term_types.question: Are message delays bounded, or can they be unbounded?
term_types.description: Classifies communication timing assumptions as synchronous with bounded delays or asynchronous with unbounded delays.

values.definition: Message delays are bounded, enabling timestamp and clock-based rules.
Message delays are unbounded, with no guaranteed delivery time.

term_types.name: Immutability and governance basis
term_types.question: How is ledger immutability maintained, and by whom can it be altered?
term_types.description: Classifies how resistant the ledger is to change and whether informal governance can alter it, as with forks.

values.definition: Records are altered only through formal protocol mechanisms with broad consensus.
Records may be changed through community-driven forks reflecting informal governance.

term_types.name: Fork type
term_types.question: Is the ledger change a backward-compatible or incompatible fork?
term_types.description: Classifies protocol changes by compatibility with existing ledger rules.

values.definition: Backward-compatible change that tightens existing rules.
Non-backward-compatible change that splits the ledger.

term_types.name: Layout effect on performance
term_types.question: How does the count of a given element class affect global system behaviour?
term_types.description: Rates how detrimental a system layout is to performance as system size grows.

values.definition: Element count does not materially affect global performance.
Global performance degrades at most in proportion to element count.
Global performance degrades at most with the square of element count.
Global performance degrades faster than quadratically with element count.

term_types.name: Scaling binding constraint
term_types.question: Which resource (transactions, users or account states, nodes, or traffic) limits the system's scalability?
term_types.description: Identifies the resource that becomes the binding limit on system scalability, distinct from how performance degrades with size.

values.definition: Throughput limited by the number of transactions processed.
Limited by the number of users or stored account states.
Limited by the number of nodes participating in the network.
Limited by the volume of network traffic generated.

term_types.name: Node data storage model
term_types.question: Do nodes hold full equivalent copies of the data, or only a subset of it?
term_types.description: Classifies whether nodes are fully equivalent replicas or thin nodes holding only part of the ledger.

values.definition: Holds a complete copy of the data and is equivalent to other peers, giving redundancy and resilience.
Holds only a subset of the data, improving scalability at some cost to resiliency.

term_types.name: Block storage content
term_types.question: Does the ledger store transactions or the resulting user balances?
term_types.description: Classifies ledgers by whether they record transaction histories or account balance states, which affects accountability and rollback ability.

values.definition: Records the transaction history itself, supporting accountability and rollback.
Records resulting user account balances rather than the full transaction history.

term_types.name: Transaction fee model
term_types.question: Is the transaction fee variable with transaction size or fixed by request type?
term_types.description: Classifies how transaction fees are priced, either scaling with transaction size or fixed per request type.

values.definition: Fees scale with transaction size, as in satoshis per byte, with priority bidding to avoid queuing.
Fees are fixed by the type of request or operation rather than its size.

term_types.name: Native currency status
term_types.question: Does the system have its own native asset, and if so how many?
term_types.description: Classifies blockchain systems by whether they issue a native cryptocurrency or convert between multiple assets.

values.definition: The system has no native asset or cryptocurrency.
The system issues its own single native cryptocurrency.
The system supports convertible multiple native assets.

term_types.name: Tokenisation provision
term_types.question: How is tokenisation provided by the system?
term_types.description: Classifies whether a system supports asset tokenisation natively or through add-ons.

values.definition: The system provides no tokenisation capability.
Tokenisation is provided through third-party add-on layers or tools.

term_types.name: Tokenisation platform blockchain environment
term_types.question: Does the tokenisation platform run on a private permissioned blockchain or a permissioned system atop a public permissionless chain?
term_types.description: Classifies tokenisation platforms by the blockchain environment on which they operate.

values.definition: Runs on a private permissioned blockchain.
Runs as a permissioned system atop a public permissionless chain.

term_types.name: Privacy-enhancing technique
term_types.question: Which technique is used to obscure transaction parties or links on a public blockchain?
term_types.description: Distinguishes privacy techniques by whether they mix transactions externally, share secrets, or add cryptographic hiding tools.

values.definition: Transactions are grouped with others through external mixing services such as CoinJoin.
Secrets are split so that a K-of-N subset is needed to reconstruct them.
Tools such as ring signatures or stealth addresses hide senders or recipients.
Privacy built into the protocol, such as ZK-SNARKs, secure multi-party computation or node-to-node encryption.

term_types.name: Data encryption and validation method
term_types.question: How is ledger data secured and validated cryptographically without disclosing underlying inputs?
term_types.description: Classifies cryptographic techniques by whether validation requires supplied public-key or data inputs.

values.definition: Validation requires the issuer's public-key or data input, as with SHA-2 hashing.
Validation proves a statement without revealing or requiring the supplied data, as with ZK-SNARKs.

term_types.name: Codebase coding language
term_types.question: Is the system implemented in one programming language or several?
term_types.description: Classifies blockchain codebases by the number of programming languages used.

values.definition: The codebase is written in one programming language.
The codebase is written in more than one programming language.

term_types.name: Scripting language expressiveness
term_types.question: How computationally general is the scripting language, and can it access data outside the blockchain?
term_types.description: Classifies on-chain scripting languages by Turing completeness and whether they draw on external data via oracles.

values.definition: Computationally general language capable of arbitrary computation, as in Ethereum.
General-purpose but non-Turing complete scripting, as in Bitcoin.
Restricted to a specific application domain and non-Turing complete, as in DAML.
Non-Turing complete language that accesses external data through oracles.

term_types.name: Protocol governance model
term_types.question: Who sets the technical rules of the system: an open community, a single firm, or an industry alliance?
term_types.description: Classifies blockchain governance by the party that defines and maintains the technical rules.

values.definition: Rules are set by an open-source community of contributors, as with Bitcoin and Ethereum.
Rules are set by a single firm offering a proprietary system.
Rules are set by an industry consortium with defined membership criteria.

term_types.name: Code license openness
term_types.question: Is the source code publicly available and open?
term_types.description: Classifies blockchain software by whether its source code is open or closed.

values.definition: Source code is publicly available under an open licence.
Source code is proprietary and not publicly available.

term_types.name: Software architecture
term_types.question: Is the codebase built as a single unit or as separable components?
term_types.description: Classifies blockchain software by whether it is monolithic or modular in design.

values.definition: The software is a single integrated unit.
The software is composed of separable interacting components.

term_types.name: Automation mechanism
term_types.question: Are transaction rules enforced automatically by self-executing code?
term_types.description: Distinguishes systems whose rules execute automatically through smart contracts from those relying on manual enforcement.

values.definition: Self-executing code enforces rules and prevents double entries automatically.
Rules are enforced through manual or intermediary processes.

term_types.name: Data storage location
term_types.question: Where is the data associated with a transaction stored?
term_types.description: Classifies whether transaction data sits on-chain within ledger limits or off-chain.

values.definition: Data is stored directly on the distributed ledger, subject to size limits.
Data is stored outside the ledger, with references or meta-coins recorded on-chain.

term_types.name: Distributed ledger definitional basis
term_types.question: Does the technology qualify as a distributed ledger, and is it a blockchain?
term_types.description: Distinguishes DLT in general from blockchain as a subtype using the statutory definitional criteria.

values.definition: A shared ledger recorded across distributed nodes without the full blockchain features.
A DLT meeting shared network ledger, cryptographic linking, automated distribution and public source code criteria.

term_types.name: Blockchain definition criteria met
term_types.question: Does the system satisfy all statutory blockchain criteria: shared, cryptographically linked, automatically distributed public ledger with public source code?
term_types.description: Tests whether a system meets the statutory blockchain definition, which requires shared, linked, distributed and publicly available source code features.

values.definition: Shared, cryptographically linked, automatically distributed public ledger with publicly available source code.
Lacks one or more of the shared, linked, distributed, or public source code features.

term_types.name: Distributed ledger component type
term_types.question: Is the distributed ledger component a protocol, application, or whole system?
term_types.description: Distinguishes distributed ledger protocols, applications, and systems as components, including blockchain applications and protocols.

values.definition: The underlying rules and shared data layer, including public source code executed by network participants.
Software built on a distributed ledger protocol, including executable smart contracts, providing user functions.
The combination of protocol, applications, and participants forming the whole ledger environment.

term_types.name: Network layer position
term_types.question: Is the network a base blockchain or a secondary network built on top of one?
term_types.description: Classifies networks by whether they are base layers or built atop another blockchain.

values.definition: A base blockchain providing its own consensus and settlement.
A network built atop a base blockchain that relies on it for settlement.

term_types.name: DeFi technology stack layer
term_types.question: Which layer of the DeFi stack does a component belong to, and what function does it perform?
term_types.description: Classifies DeFi architecture components by the functional layer they occupy, from base settlement to user interface.

values.definition: User-facing layer through which users interact with protocols.
Layer that transmits transactions and messages between participants and the network.
Layer of self-executing contracts implementing protocol logic.
Layer representing tokenised assets recorded on the stack.
Underlying chain layer providing final settlement and consensus.

term_types.name: Network decentralisation status
term_types.question: Is the network sufficiently decentralised that no person or group controls its governance?
term_types.description: Classifies a network by whether its governance and operation are free from control by a person or group.

values.definition: Transparent rules-based system with participation not controlled by any person or group under common control.
Governance is controlled by a person or group under common control.

term_types.name: Decentralisation test outcome
term_types.question: Can any person unilaterally alter rules, and do holdings, voting power or source-code changes exceed control thresholds over the test period?
term_types.description: Applies quantitative and unilateral-control tests (such as 20 percent holdings or voting power thresholds) to determine decentralisation.

values.definition: No person can unilaterally alter rules, and no holder exceeds control thresholds over the test periods.
A person can unilaterally alter rules, or holdings, voting power or source-code changes exceed thresholds.

term_types.name: Decentralised finance trading protocol status
term_types.question: Is the system a decentralised finance trading protocol operating on predetermined, non-discretionary rules without intermediaries or common control?
term_types.description: Determines whether a blockchain system qualifies as a DeFi trading protocol, which requires predetermined rules, no reliance on intermediaries, and absence of common control.

values.definition: Blockchain system with predetermined, non-discretionary rules, no intermediary reliance, and not under common control.
Under common control, not governed solely by encoded rules, or relies on intermediaries.

term_types.name: Decentralised finance messaging system status
term_types.question: Is the software a messaging system that lets users submit instructions to a protocol without third-party control over funds or execution?
term_types.description: Distinguishes DeFi messaging software that merely relays user instructions from software that gives third parties control over funds or execution.

values.definition: Software letting users submit instructions to a protocol, without third parties controlling funds or execution.
Gives third parties control over funds or execution, so falls outside the messaging definition.

term_types.name: Wallet signing arrangement
term_types.question: Is a wallet single-signature or multiple-signature, and how is signing authority split among keys?
term_types.description: Distinguishes single-signature from multiple-signature and multi-party computation wallet arrangements.

values.definition: A single key controls the wallet's assets.
Multiple keys are required to authorise transactions, possibly held by different parties.
Signing authority is split across parties via cryptographic computation rather than discrete keys.

term_types.name: Wallet connectivity
term_types.question: Is the wallet connected to the internet, trading security against speed?
term_types.description: Classifies wallets by whether their keys are held online, trading speed against security.

values.definition: Wallet keys are held online and connected to the internet, enabling faster transfers.
Wallet keys are held offline, offering greater security but slower transfers.

term_types.name: DLT access permission basis
term_types.question: Can any party participate without approval, or does participation require approval by an authority?
term_types.description: Classifies a DLT system by whether participation is permissionless or requires authority approval, after confirming it meets the distributed ledger definition.

values.definition: Any party can participate without approval.
Participation requires approval by an authority.

term_types.name: Quantum threat exposure
term_types.question: Does the system rely on public-key cryptography exposed to quantum attack, and can it migrate to standardised post-quantum algorithms?
term_types.description: Classifies systems by exposure to quantum threats against their public-key cryptography, and by readiness for post-quantum migration.

values.definition: Relies on public-key cryptography vulnerable to quantum attacks that could expose private keys.
Uses or can migrate to standardised post-quantum algorithms such as NIST FIPS 203, 204 or 205.

term_types.name: Cryptographic agility
term_types.question: Can the platform replace cryptographic algorithms without disrupting operations?
term_types.description: Classifies platforms by their capacity to swap algorithms for migration or to retire weak ones.

values.definition: Can replace algorithms without disrupting operations, supporting migration and retirement of weak algorithms.
Algorithm replacement would disrupt operations or is impractical, for example due to immutability or public-key reuse.

term_types.name: Node role
term_types.question: Does the node validate transactions, record data, or commit blocks?
term_types.description: Classifies network nodes by their role in recording, validating, and committing data.

values.definition: Records data on the ledger.
Validates transactions or commits transaction blocks.

term_types.name: Asset definitional basis
term_types.question: Is the asset defined by its underlying technology or by its use case?
term_types.description: Distinguishes definitions that classify assets by the ledger technology they are recorded on from use-case definitions.

values.definition: Defined by being a digital representation of value recorded on a distributed ledger.
Defined by the function or purpose the asset serves in transactions.

term_types.name: Fungibility
term_types.question: Is the asset interchangeable unit for unit with others of its kind?
term_types.description: Separates fungible digital assets from non-fungible units such as NFTs.

values.definition: Units are interchangeable and equivalent to one another.
Each unit is unique and not interchangeable with other units.

term_types.name: Asset technical standard
term_types.question: Is the token native to its chain or a smart-contract standard token, and is it fungible or non-fungible?
term_types.description: Classifies tokens by the technical standard they follow, distinguishing native chain assets from contract-based fungible or non-fungible standards.

values.definition: Native asset of its own chain, such as BTC or ETH.
Fungible token issued via smart contract, such as an ERC-20 token.
Unique token issued under a non-fungible standard such as ERC-721.

term_types.name: Virtual asset status
term_types.question: Does the digital representation of value fall within the virtual asset definition, or is it another financial asset?
term_types.description: Determines whether an item is a virtual asset, excluded fiat or securities representation, or other financial asset.

values.definition: A digital representation of value that can be traded, transferred, and used for payment or investment.
A digital representation of fiat currency or securities already covered elsewhere, excluded from the VA definition.
A blockchain-based asset classed as a financial asset rather than a virtual asset, judged by function rather than technology.

term_types.name: Qualifying cryptoasset scope
term_types.question: Is the cryptoasset fungible and transferable, and not solely a record of value or contractual rights?
term_types.description: Tests whether a cryptoasset qualifies under the regulatory definition, excluding specified investments, e-money, currency and limited-network tokens.

values.definition: Fungible and transferable, not solely a record of value or contractual rights, and not excluded investment, e-money or currency.
Fails the fungibility or transferability tests, or falls within an excluded investment, e-money, currency or limited-network category.

term_types.name: Legal tender status
term_types.question: Does the asset have legal tender status?
term_types.description: Distinguishes virtual currency that lacks legal tender status from currency with legal tender status.

values.definition: Recognised as legal tender by a sovereign authority.
Operates as a medium of exchange without legal tender status.

term_types.name: Convertibility and currency substitution
term_types.question: Does the asset have equivalent value to currency or substitute for it?
term_types.description: Identifies convertible virtual currency by whether it functions as a substitute for currency.

values.definition: Has equivalent value to currency or substitutes for currency in transactions.
Does not have equivalent value to currency or substitute for it.

term_types.name: Value substitute for currency
term_types.question: Is the value a substitute for currency, whether created for that use or repurposed by an administrator?
term_types.description: Determines whether value that may not involve funds functions as a currency substitute, either originally or by repurposing.

values.definition: Functions as a substitute for currency, either created for that use or repurposed by an administrator.
Does not function as a substitute for currency.

term_types.name: Minting mechanism
term_types.question: How does the crypto-asset originate?
term_types.description: Classifies crypto-assets by how units are created.

values.definition: Units are minted as rewards for consensus work, stake, or similar validation.
Units are minted against locked collateral held elsewhere.
Units represent tokens locked in staking and issued as receipts.
Units represent another asset held in custody and issued on a different chain.
Units are created and destroyed according to an algorithmic equilibrium.
Units are created through governance decisions or scheduled emission.
Units are created and allocated before or at launch.
Unique tokens are created to represent individual items or rights.

term_types.name: Issuer presence
term_types.question: Is there a single identifiable issuer, a protocol issuer, or no issuer?
term_types.description: Classifies the issuer arrangement behind a crypto-asset.

values.definition: A single identifiable legal entity creates and controls issuance.
Units are issued according to protocol rules without a controlling entity.
No party issues the asset; it arises from network activity or mining.

term_types.name: Yield type
term_types.question: Does the asset return capital appreciation, yield, or neither?
term_types.description: Separates capital appreciation from yield and classifies yield by its source.

values.definition: Return arises from increase in the market value of the asset.
Return is paid from lending, liquidity fees, staking, or revenue sharing.
Return is paid through emission-based or burn-and-mint incentives.
The asset generates neither capital appreciation nor yield by design.

term_types.name: Yield distribution mechanism
term_types.question: How is yield delivered to holders: by increasing quantity, value, or price, or by external redistribution?
term_types.description: Classifies how yield reaches holders, distinguishing rebasing quantity accrual, value accrual, price accrual, and external redistribution.

values.definition: Holder balances increase in quantity over time, as with rebasing tokens.
Yield accrues to the value of each unit held without changing quantity.
Yield is realised through an increase in the market price of the token.
Yield is paid out to holders from revenue or fees redistributed externally.

term_types.name: Control model
term_types.question: Who controls governance, issuance, yield, and redemption?
term_types.description: Classifies crypto-assets as centralised, decentralised, or hybrid by who holds control.

values.definition: A single legal entity controls governance, issuance, yield, and redemption.
Control is distributed across protocol participants without a controlling entity.
Control is shared between a legal entity and protocol mechanisms.

term_types.name: Economic function
term_types.question: What economic role does the token play for its holders?
term_types.description: Separates tokens by their economic function as governance, utility, or security instruments.

values.definition: Confers voting or governance rights over a protocol or network.
Provides access to a good or service on a platform, as defined under MiCAR.
Qualifies as a financial instrument under MiFID II.

term_types.name: Holder rights form
term_types.question: Are holder rights contractual or property-type, and is the claim against the issuer's balance sheet or a segregated reserve?
term_types.description: Classifies the legal form of holder rights along personal versus property and balance-sheet versus segregated-reserve axes, relevant to insolvency and credit exposure.

values.definition: Contractual claim against the issuer's general balance sheet.
Contractual claim against a segregated reserve of backing assets.
Property-type right with claim against the issuer's balance sheet.
Property-type right backed by a segregated reserve of assets.
Holder has no claim on the issuer or any reserve.

term_types.name: Redemption mechanism
term_types.question: How and by whom can holders redeem or exit the asset for its underlying value?
term_types.description: Classifies redemption by whether it is custodial, on-chain, market-based, or queued.

values.definition: Redemption is handled off-chain by a custodian that burns or locks the underlying asset.
Holders exit by selling the asset on a market rather than redeeming with the issuer.
Redemption is processed by the protocol through a scheduled withdrawal queue.
The protocol redeems units at par through a built-in mechanism.
Holders redeem a claim against a pool of underlying assets.
Smart contract releases the underlying upon burning of the token.
Cross-chain bridge burns tokens on one chain and releases the underlying on another.

term_types.name: Redemption reference asset type
term_types.question: What does the asset's redemption right or value reference: fiat, physical or collateral assets, other tokens, or nothing?
term_types.description: Classifies tokens by the asset that redemption or the stable value refers to, including fiat-pegged, asset-referenced, and non-stablecoin redeemable forms.

values.definition: Redeemable or pegged to one or more fiat currencies, such as EMTs or payment stablecoins.
Redeemable for physical commodities or collateral assets, such as ARTs.
Not a stablecoin but with redemption features, such as wrapped or liquid staking tokens.
Has no redemption feature with any reference asset.

term_types.name: Redemption legal character
term_types.question: Does redemption create a legal claim, a regulatory obligation, or only market exposure?
term_types.description: Distinguishes whether redemption rights give a legal claim, regulatory obligation, or only market exposure.

values.definition: Holders have an enforceable legal claim against an issuer or custodian for redemption.
Redemption is subject to a regulatory obligation on the issuer.
Holders have no enforceable redemption right, only exposure to market price.

term_types.name: Securities classification
term_types.question: Is the asset a security or financial instrument under the applicable test?
term_types.description: Classifies whether an asset is an investment contract or financial instrument under tests such as Howey or MiFID.

values.definition: Qualifies as an investment contract or financial instrument under the applicable test.
Does not satisfy the investment contract or financial instrument criteria.

term_types.name: Digital asset security category
term_types.question: Does the digital asset fall within a listed security, security derivative, or other instrument category?
term_types.description: Classifies digital assets against the security definitions, including investment contracts, security derivatives, and other listed instrument categories.

values.definition: Investment contract, note, or profit-sharing interest giving ownership, creditor, or income rights.
Security futures, security-based swaps, or options on securities.
Qualifies as a permitted payment stablecoin, excluded from security status.
Commodity or commodity derivative under the applicable definition.
Banking deposit or account instrument.
Interest in a pooled investment vehicle.
Goods, collectibles or other non-commodity assets.

term_types.name: Digital asset ownership and creditor rights
term_types.question: Does the asset give holders an ownership, creditor, interest or income right in an enterprise?
term_types.description: Determines whether the asset gives holders an ownership interest, creditor interest, or right to interest or principal, relevant to security status.

values.definition: Gives holders an ownership or creditor interest, or a right to interest or principal.
Does not give holders ownership, creditor interest or income rights in an enterprise.

term_types.name: Digital commodity status
term_types.question: Is the asset a digital commodity under the applicable framework?
term_types.description: Determines whether an asset is a digital commodity, versus a security or other asset, including tests of intrinsic blockchain linkage and functional use.

values.definition: Intrinsically linked to a blockchain system and value derived from its programmatic functioning.
Does not meet the criteria for a digital commodity.

term_types.name: Digital commodity value source
term_types.question: Is the asset's value derived from the programmatic functioning of its network or from others' managerial efforts?
term_types.description: Distinguishes assets whose value comes from a network's programmatic operation from those whose value depends on others' managerial or entrepreneurial efforts.

values.definition: Value derived from the programmatic functioning of a network.
Value dependent on the managerial or entrepreneurial efforts of others.

term_types.name: Intrinsic blockchain linkage
term_types.question: Is the digital asset intrinsically linked to a blockchain system, with functional uses such as fees, governance or incentives within it?
term_types.description: Tests whether an asset's value and uses are tied to a blockchain system, the basis of the digital commodity definition.

values.definition: Functional uses such as fees, governance or incentives arise within the blockchain system.
No intrinsic functional link to a blockchain system.

term_types.name: Legal asset category
term_types.question: Which legal category does the asset fall into among securities, stablecoins, funds, and other crypto-assets?
term_types.description: Sorts assets into legal categories using the Howey, MiFID, ART/AIF, and MiCAR stablecoin tests.

values.definition: Securities or financial instruments under Howey or MiFID tests.
Asset-referenced or e-money token with a stable value purpose under MiCAR.
Asset meeting the ART or AIF test for pooled investment.
Crypto-asset or commodity not falling into the above categories.

term_types.name: Stable value purpose
term_types.question: Is the asset designed to maintain a stable value against a reference?
term_types.description: Identifies whether the asset's purpose is to hold a stable value relative to a reference asset.

values.definition: Designed to maintain stable value by referencing fiat, commodities, or other assets.
Not designed to maintain a stable value against any reference.

term_types.name: Reference asset type
term_types.question: What does the asset's value reference or track?
term_types.description: Classifies stable-value tokens and other assets by the reference they are pegged or tracked against.

values.definition: Value is referenced to one or more fiat currencies.
Value is referenced to a physical or digital commodity.
Value is referenced to other crypto-assets.
No external reference; value maintained algorithmically or not referenced.

term_types.name: Reserve backing type
term_types.question: What reserves back the stable-value token?
term_types.description: Classifies stable-value tokens by the composition of their backing reserves.

values.definition: Backed by fiat currency reserves.
Backed by crypto-asset collateral.
Backed by commodity reserves.
Not backed by reserves; maintained by algorithm or other means.

term_types.name: Stablecoin classification conditions
term_types.question: Do the redemption rights, reserves and network design meet the conditions for a stabilised stablecoin?
term_types.description: Tests whether a stablecoin's redemption terms, risk management, and network design satisfy the classification conditions.

values.definition: Redemption, risk management, network design and redeemer regulation meet the classification conditions.
One or more classification conditions are not satisfied.

term_types.name: Stablecoin redemption and reserve test
term_types.question: Do reserves cover the peg value and consist of low-risk, liquid assets with enforceable redemption?
term_types.description: Tests whether a stablecoin's reserves at all times equal or exceed the peg value, are low-risk and liquid, and back legally enforceable redemption.

values.definition: Reserves cover peg value at all times, are low-risk and liquid, with enforceable redemption and disclosure.
Reserves fall short of peg value, are not low-risk or liquid, or redemption is not enforceable.

term_types.name: Stablecoin issuer prudential supervision
term_types.question: Is the stablecoin issuer supervised under prudential capital and liquidity rules?
term_types.description: Determines whether the issuer is subject to prudential capital and liquidity supervision as a classification condition for stablecoins.

values.definition: Issuer is supervised under prudential capital and liquidity rules.
Issuer is not subject to prudential capital and liquidity supervision.

term_types.name: Stablecoin freeze capability
term_types.question: Can the issuer freeze, block or burn stablecoin units under lawful orders?
term_types.description: Distinguishes stablecoin issuers retaining freeze, block and burn capability from freeze-resistant designs.

values.definition: Issuer retains freeze, block and burn capability over units.
Design prevents freezing, blocking or burning of units.

term_types.name: Permitted payment stablecoin status
term_types.question: Does the stablecoin meet the permitted payment stablecoin criteria for payment use, redemption, and issuer regulation?
term_types.description: Determines whether a stablecoin qualifies as a permitted payment stablecoin under the statutory criteria.

values.definition: Used or designed for payment or settlement, with issuer redemption obligation, regulated issuer, and not a national currency or registered security.
Fails one or more permitted payment stablecoin criteria.

term_types.name: Permitted payment stablecoin issuer category
term_types.question: Is the issuer an insured depository institution subsidiary, a federal qualified issuer, or a state qualified issuer?
term_types.description: Classifies permitted payment stablecoin issuers by institutional category, which determines the primary federal regulator.

values.definition: Subsidiary of an insured depository institution issuing payment stablecoins.
Non-bank issuer qualified under federal authority.
Non-bank issuer qualified under a state regime.

term_types.name: Stablecoin arrangement function status
term_types.question: Does the party redeem, transfer, store or settle the stablecoin, and is it regulated?
term_types.description: Classifies parties executing stablecoin redemption, transfer, storage or settlement by whether they are regulated.

values.definition: Entity executing redemption, transfer, storage or settlement that is regulated or subject to appropriate risk standards.
Entity executing these functions without regulation or appropriate risk standards.

term_types.name: Stablecoin arrangement participant role
term_types.question: Is the party a validator, cloud host, hardware maker, merchant, or software developer without VASP functions?
term_types.description: Identifies parties in a stablecoin arrangement that generally fall outside VASP status.

values.definition: Participates only in validation of the network.
Provides cloud hosting services only.
Manufactures hardware or unhosted wallet software.
Accepts virtual assets as payment for goods or services.
Develops software without performing VASP functions.

term_types.name: Restricted digital asset status
term_types.question: Is the digital asset restricted by holder status, acquisition channel, and blockchain decentralisation?
term_types.description: Determines whether a digital asset is restricted based on holder, acquisition channel, and blockchain status, excluding permitted payment stablecoins.

values.definition: Held by a related person or acquired through distribution, and blockchain is not certified decentralised.
Does not meet the restricted digital asset criteria.

term_types.name: Network maturity status
term_types.question: Has the network reached mature decentralised governance such that the asset is no longer subject to issuer-based treatment?
term_types.description: Distinguishes assets where a network has matured to decentralised governance from those where an issuer retains control.

values.definition: Network has reached maturity with decentralised governance; no controlling issuer.
Network is not yet mature or an issuer retains control of operations.

term_types.name: Digital asset issuance or distribution activity
term_types.question: Is the asset issued or distributed through an ICO, pre-sale, airdrop, or end-user distribution?
term_types.description: Classifies initial issuance and distribution activities such as ICOs, pre-sales, airdrops, and end-user distributions.

values.definition: Initial coin offering of digital assets to the public.
Pre-sale arrangement such as SAFT, equity-plus-token warrant or convertible note with token purchase option.
Gratuitous or nominal-consideration transfer, including transfers triggered by forks.
Distribution with no more than nominal value exchanged and broad, equitable access, including protocol staking.

term_types.name: Mature system end user distribution status
term_types.question: Were all units issued through programmatic functioning as end user distributions, and was the asset marketed to the public as an investment?
term_types.description: Tests whether an asset's distribution history and marketing qualify it as end-user distribution for mature blockchain treatment.

values.definition: All units in the prior twelve months were end user distributions and the asset was not marketed as an investment.
Units were not all end user distributions or the asset was marketed to the public as an investment.

term_types.name: Securities registration status
term_types.question: Must the digital asset offering be registered under the Securities Act or exempt?
term_types.description: Classifies digital asset offerings by whether they require registration or qualify for an exemption.

values.definition: Offering requires Securities Act registration.
Offering qualifies for an exemption such as Regulation D, A, S or Crowdfunding.
Non-security digital asset falling outside a comprehensive U.S. framework.

term_types.name: Regulated crypto-asset issuance or service perimeter
term_types.question: Is the offering, admission or service performed for others by a regulated entity within the framework's perimeter?
term_types.description: Determines whether an issuance, admission, or service activity falls within the regulated perimeter of the framework.

values.definition: Activity performed for others within the regulated perimeter.
Activity outside the regulated perimeter or excluded by exemption.

term_types.name: Tokenised asset status
term_types.question: Does the tokenised asset carry the same risks and legal rights as its traditional form?
term_types.description: Determines whether a tokenised traditional asset retains the credit, market and legal rights of its traditional counterpart.

values.definition: Carries the same credit and market risk and legal rights as the traditional asset.
Carries different risk or legal rights from its traditional form.

term_types.name: Tokenised asset type
term_types.question: Is the tokenised asset a financial asset or a non-financial one?
term_types.description: Separates tokenised financial assets such as fund shares or private credit from non-financial assets such as art or receivables.

values.definition: Tokenised money market fund shares, bank deposits or private credit.
Tokenised trade receivables, art or collectibles.

term_types.name: Ledger record type
term_types.question: Is the asset recorded on a public, cryptographically secured ledger accessible without an intermediary?
term_types.description: Classifies assets by whether their transfer is recorded on a public ledger and transferable without intermediaries.

values.definition: Recorded on a public, cryptographically secured ledger and transferable without intermediaries.
Recorded on a private ledger or transferred only through an intermediary.

term_types.name: Asset classification in fund and securities context
term_types.question: Is the blockchain-based asset classed as a security, fund unit or other financial asset under the applicable test?
term_types.description: Determines whether a blockchain-based asset falls within the financial asset categories, such as securities or fund interests, rather than virtual asset regulation.

values.definition: Classed as a security or fund interest under the applicable test.
Classed as a financial asset other than a security or fund interest.
Not a financial asset and covered under virtual asset guidance.

term_types.name: Funds or assets category
term_types.question: Does the item fall within the broad definition of funds or other assets?
term_types.description: Identifies whether an asset is covered by the broad, non-exhaustive definition of funds or other assets.

values.definition: Within the broad definition of funds or other assets covered by the framework.
Outside the funds or other assets definition.

term_types.name: High-value goods status
term_types.question: Is the good a high-value good, precious metal or stone, or cultural good?
term_types.description: Classifies goods by whether they fall in high-value, precious metal or stone, or cultural goods categories.

values.definition: Good of high value within the AML framework definition.
Precious metal or stone within the AML framework definition.
Cultural good within the AML framework definition.
Good falling outside these categories.

term_types.name: Legal entity identification status
term_types.question: Does the party have a standard legal entity identifier conforming to ISO 17442?
term_types.description: Records whether a party is identified by an ISO 17442 legal entity identifier.

values.definition: Assigned a unique ISO 17442 legal entity identifier.
No legal entity identifier assigned, or an identifier not conforming to ISO 17442.

term_types.name: Transfer party role
term_types.question: What role does a party play in a crypto-asset transfer?
term_types.description: Identifies the originator, beneficiary, or intermediary role of a party in a transfer.

values.definition: The holder of the account, address, or device from which the transfer is made, or the initiator where none exists.
The intended recipient of the crypto-asset transfer.
A payment service provider or other provider that handles a transfer between originator and beneficiary.

term_types.name: Originator account type
term_types.question: Does the originator hold a crypto-asset account, distributed ledger address, or storage device?
term_types.description: Classifies the originator by whether they control a crypto-asset account, ledger address, or device.

values.definition: Holds a crypto-asset account, distributed ledger address, or storage device from which transfer is made.
Orders or initiates the transfer where no account, address or device exists.

term_types.name: VASP-covered business activity
term_types.question: Which listed service does the business perform for others?
term_types.description: Identifies which of the five listed VASP activities a business conducts for others.

values.definition: Exchange between virtual assets and fiat currencies.
Exchange between one or more forms of virtual assets.
Transfer of virtual assets from one address or account to another on behalf of others.
Safekeeping or administration of virtual assets or instruments enabling control.
Participation in an issuer's offer or sale of a virtual asset.

term_types.name: Exchange and trading service model
term_types.question: How does the trading or exchange service operate?
term_types.description: Classifies exchange and trading services by model, from escrow and brokerage to order-book and advanced trading.

values.definition: Provider holds custody of funds during the exchange.
Provider issues or trades virtual assets for users.
Platform matches buy and sell orders, excluding pure matching platforms performing no listed service.
Provides margin, algorithmic, or other advanced trading services.
Exchange conducted through physical kiosks accepting or dispensing currency or virtual assets.

term_types.name: Trading platform possession
term_types.question: Does the platform take possession of the convertible virtual currency between buyers and sellers?
term_types.description: Distinguishes bid-offer posting venues from exchangers that buy and sell CVC themselves.

values.definition: Platform posts bids and offers, leaving settlement to parties through outside wallets.
Platform buys from sellers and sells to buyers, taking possession of the CVC.

term_types.name: Custody and control capability
term_types.question: Can the entity hold, trade, transfer or spend a virtual asset, or enable control through keys or contracts?
term_types.description: Tests whether an entity has custody or control capacity over virtual assets, including via multi-signature or smart contracts.

values.definition: Entity can hold, trade, transfer or spend virtual assets, or enable control through keys or smart contracts.
Entity lacks the ability to hold, transfer or control virtual assets for others.

term_types.name: Custody arrangement
term_types.question: Who holds the keys or controls the asset: a custodian or the user?
term_types.description: Classifies wallets and providers as custodial or non-custodial by who controls the private keys.

values.definition: A third party holds the keys and controls the asset on the user's behalf.
The user alone controls the keys and the asset.

term_types.name: Custody provider type
term_types.question: Is the custodian a regulated institution or an unregulated custody provider?
term_types.description: Classifies custodians by whether they are regulated banks, trusts, or other custody providers.

values.definition: A bank or state-chartered trust providing custody under regulatory supervision.
A custody provider without a bank or trust charter.
The holder safeguards its own assets without a third-party custodian.

term_types.name: Wallet custodial control
term_types.question: Can the wallet provider unilaterally move client assets?
term_types.description: Classifies wallets as custodial or non-custodial by whether the provider can unilaterally transfer client assets.

values.definition: Provider can unilaterally move client assets.
Provider cannot unilaterally move client assets.

term_types.name: Cryptoasset safeguarding control
term_types.question: Does the party hold or store means of access, or appoint a custodian to do so?
term_types.description: Assesses control over cryptoassets for safeguarding by holding or storing access means, or by appointing a custodian.

values.definition: Holds or stores the means of access, such as a private cryptographic key.
Appoints another party to hold or store the means of access.

term_types.name: Peer-to-peer platform function
term_types.question: Does the peer-to-peer platform merely provide a forum or perform matching or finding services?
term_types.description: Classifies P2P platforms by whether they are a minimal forum or actively match and find counterparties.

values.definition: Provides only a forum or communication means with no matching or finding function.
Actively matches or finds counterparties and may qualify as a VASP.

term_types.name: Operator control and profit
term_types.question: Who profits, sets rules, controls operations, or could shut down the service?
term_types.description: Captures the control and profit factors used to determine whether an actor is in substance an operator.

values.definition: Party sets and changes rules, controls operations, profits, or could shut the service down.
Party lacks control, profit or shutdown power and is peripheral to the service.

term_types.name: Software developer VASP status
term_types.question: Does the developer or platform creator retain control or influence over assets or user relationships?
term_types.description: Separates software developers and platform creators from parties retaining control or influence that may make them VASPs, including through protocol parameters or ongoing user relationships.

values.definition: Builds or sells software without retaining control or influence over assets or user relationships.
Retains control or influence over assets, protocol parameters or user relationships, and may be a VASP.

term_types.name: Ancillary provider status
term_types.question: Does the provider facilitate covered activities for others, or only supply hardware, software or network infrastructure?
term_types.description: Identifies ancillary providers, such as hardware wallet makers and infrastructure operators, excluded from VASP status unless they facilitate covered activities.

values.definition: Supplies hardware, unhosted wallet software or network infrastructure without facilitating covered activities for others.
Facilitates covered VA activities for others and may fall within scope.

term_types.name: Digital asset infrastructure function
term_types.question: What infrastructure function does the provider perform?
term_types.description: Sorts digital asset infrastructure providers by the function they perform.

values.definition: Supplies offchain data to onchain systems.
Aggregates liquidity across decentralised exchanges.
Enables cross-chain asset transfers.
Grants network access by operating nodes.
Provides blockchain-derived data to users.
Provides identity verification for network participants.
Audits smart contract code for vulnerabilities.
Operates user-facing interfaces to underlying protocols.

term_types.name: ICO participation type
term_types.question: How is the business involved in the initial coin offering?
term_types.description: Distinguishes issuing a virtual asset from exchange, transfer, or safekeeping activity in ICOs.

values.definition: Issuing a virtual asset alone, which is not a covered service.
Accepting orders, purchasing for resale, underwriting, market making or placing tokens on behalf of others.
Creating issuance software alone, which does not make a developer a VASP.

term_types.name: Token sale business model
term_types.question: Is the token sale a preferential group sale or an equity or debt token fundraise?
term_types.description: Classifies token sales by business model, which determines money transmitter or exemption status.

values.definition: Seller acting as administrator sells CVC to a preferential group.
Tokens represent equity or debt used to fund projects.

term_types.name: Trading venue type
term_types.question: Is the digital asset trade executed on a centralised or decentralised venue?
term_types.description: Classifies digital asset trading by venue as centralised or decentralised.

values.definition: Trading executed through a centralised exchange operator.
Trading executed through a decentralised exchange protocol.

term_types.name: Trading product type
term_types.question: Is the trade spot, futures, perpetual, or an option?
term_types.description: Classifies digital asset trades by the product being traded.

values.definition: Immediate exchange of the asset at current price.
Agreement to trade at a future date at an agreed price.
Derivative without expiry date, settled periodically.
Right but not obligation to buy or sell at a set price.

term_types.name: Order type
term_types.question: Is the order executed at market price, at a limit, or triggered by a stop?
term_types.description: Classifies trade orders by execution condition.

values.definition: Executed immediately at the best available price.
Executed only at a specified price or better.
Triggered when a specified price threshold is reached.

term_types.name: Staking participation model
term_types.question: Does the holder operate a validator, use a service, use liquid staking, or delegate via contract?
term_types.description: Classifies staking arrangements by who operates validation and whether control of tokens is retained.

values.definition: Holder runs its own validator node and retains control of tokens.
Third party operates validation on the holder's behalf.
Holder receives a receipt token representing staked assets.
Holder delegates tokens to a smart contract for staking.

term_types.name: Staking control retention
term_types.question: Does the holder retain control of tokens during staking?
term_types.description: Determines whether control of staked tokens stays with the holder or passes to a third party.

values.definition: Holder keeps control of the tokens throughout staking.
A third party controls the staked tokens or transmits funds.

term_types.name: Staking service status
term_types.question: Is the cryptoasset used in blockchain validation through a staking arrangement that is a regulated activity?
term_types.description: Determines whether using a cryptoasset to participate in validation, including proof-of-stake, falls within regulated staking.

values.definition: Using a cryptoasset in blockchain validation, including proof-of-stake, offered as a regulated service.
Excluded from regulated staking, such as protocol-level or technical services not held out to the public.

term_types.name: Slashing exposure
term_types.question: Are validators penalised for misbehaviour through loss of staked tokens?
term_types.description: Records whether a staking arrangement exposes stake to slashing penalties.

values.definition: Staked tokens may be penalised for validator misbehaviour.
No slashing penalties apply to staked tokens.

term_types.name: Transaction sequencing and MEV exposure
term_types.question: Is the transaction exposed to maximal extractable value through sequencing?
term_types.description: Classifies transactions by exposure to maximal extractable value arising from ordering control.

values.definition: Transaction ordering allows value extraction by sequencers or validators.
Transaction ordering is designed to resist value extraction.

term_types.name: Crypto-asset service scope
term_types.question: Does the service fall within the crypto-asset services category or is it excluded (such as advice)?
term_types.description: Determines whether a crypto-asset activity is within regulated crypto-asset services or excluded.

values.definition: Listed crypto-asset service performed for others under MiCAR.
Activity excluded from crypto-asset services, such as advice.

term_types.name: Incidental activity exclusion
term_types.question: Is the crypto activity merely incidental to a profession, with no systematic income and under professional supervision?
term_types.description: Determines whether an activity carried out incidentally to another profession is excluded from regulated crypto-asset activity.

values.definition: Ancillary to the profession, not a regulated activity, no systematic income, not marketed, and supervised by a professional body.
Fails one or more of the incidental activity tests.

term_types.name: Stablecoin issuance activity
term_types.question: Is the party offering, creating within a group, or redeeming and holding reserves for a qualifying stablecoin?
term_types.description: Classifies the issuance-related undertakings that constitute the regulated stablecoin issuing activity.

values.definition: Offering a qualifying stablecoin to the public.
Creating a qualifying stablecoin within a group.
Undertaking redemption or holding reserves for a qualifying stablecoin.

term_types.name: Cryptoasset trading activity
term_types.question: Is the party operating a trading platform or dealing as principal in cryptoassets?
term_types.description: Classifies regulated cryptoasset trading activities as platform operation or principal dealing.

values.definition: Operating a qualifying cryptoasset trading platform.
Dealing in qualifying cryptoassets as principal.

term_types.name: Cryptoasset dealing mode
term_types.question: Does the party deal in cryptoassets as principal or as agent, or arrange deals for others?
term_types.description: Classifies specified cryptoasset dealing and arranging activities by whether the party trades on its own account, as agent, or only arranges transactions.

values.definition: Buying or selling cryptoassets on its own account, such as market making or underwriting.
Buying or selling cryptoassets on behalf of clients.
Arranging or facilitating a transaction without itself becoming a party.

term_types.name: Digital commodity intermediary role
term_types.question: Does the person act as a broker, dealer, exchange, or custodian of digital commodities?
term_types.description: Classifies persons by whether they broker orders, act as counterparty, operate an exchange, or hold digital commodities for others.

values.definition: Holds customer funds or executes customer transactions, or solicits or accepts customer orders on a registered entity.
Regularly acts as a counterparty and holds counterparty funds.
Operates a cash or spot market for digital commodities.
Holds digital commodities for others.

term_types.name: Associated person of a digital commodity intermediary
term_types.question: Is the person an associated person of a digital commodity broker or dealer through solicitation, order acceptance or supervisory roles, excluding purely clerical functions?
term_types.description: Determines whether a person is an associated person of a digital commodity broker or dealer based on solicitation, order acceptance, or supervisory functions.

values.definition: Solicits or accepts orders or contracts, or holds a supervisory role, for a digital commodity broker or dealer.
Performs only purely clerical or ministerial functions, or has no solicitation, order or supervisory role.

term_types.name: Mixed digital asset transaction
term_types.question: Does the trade exchange a digital commodity for a security?
term_types.description: Identifies mixed transactions where a digital commodity is traded against a security.

values.definition: Trade of a digital commodity for a security.
Trade not involving a digital commodity-for-security exchange.

term_types.name: Digital commodity dealer market role
term_types.question: Does the person hold itself out as a dealer or market maker, or is it a registered or excluded counterparty?
term_types.description: Distinguishes persons dealing or making markets in digital commodities from those excluded such as eligible contract participants or validators.

values.definition: Holds itself out as a dealer or market maker, or runs a dealing business as principal in cash or spot digital commodity markets.
Excluded as trading with eligible contract participants, on registered exchanges, for own account, for payments, or validating nodes.

term_types.name: Affiliation with a digital commodity issuer
term_types.question: Does the person have control, common control, or a 5% or greater holding relationship with the issuer or asset?
term_types.description: Classifies persons by their control or ownership relationship to a digital commodity issuer or to the digital asset.

values.definition: Controls or is under common control with the issuer, or holds 5% or more of outstanding units, or is a founder or recent executive.
Lacks control, common control or the 5% holding relationship with the issuer or asset.

term_types.name: Digital asset service provider status
term_types.question: Does the person perform listed exchange, transfer, custody or issuance services for compensation in U.S. business, excluding protocol developers and validators?
term_types.description: Determines whether a person is a digital asset service provider under compensation, U.S. business, and listed-function criteria.

values.definition: Performs listed exchange, transfer, custody or issuance services for compensation in U.S. business.
Excluded as protocol developer, validator, self-custodial interface, or liquidity pool participant.

term_types.name: Travel Rule transfer type
term_types.question: Is the transaction a transmittal of funds subject to the Travel Rule, and what is its value?
term_types.description: Classifies transactions by type and dollar equivalent to determine Travel Rule applicability.

values.definition: Transaction subject to the Travel Rule requirements, based on host position in the chain.
Transaction not qualifying as transmittal of funds under the Travel Rule.

term_types.name: Transfer channel type
term_types.question: Is the transfer a credit transfer, direct debit, remittance, card or device-based transfer, or person-to-person transfer?
term_types.description: Classifies transfers of funds by payment channel and whether a service provider is involved.

values.definition: Transfer initiated by the payer's payment service provider to the payee's provider.
Transfer initiated by the payee to debit the payer's account.
Transfer of funds with no payment account at either end.
Transfer made using a card, device or similar digital or telecom instrument.
Transfer between persons without the involvement of a service provider.

term_types.name: Business relationship type
term_types.question: Is the relationship a professional connection with expected repetition or duration, or a linked set of transactions?
term_types.description: Classifies customer relationships and linked transactions by their professional or transactional character.

values.definition: Professional connection with expected repetition or duration.
Transactions sharing origin, destination, purpose and period.
Banking or crypto-asset service relationship between institutions.

term_types.name: Illicit actor type
term_types.question: Which kind of criminal or state-linked actor uses virtual assets for illicit activity?
term_types.description: Classifies actors engaged in illicit virtual asset use, such as organised crime, state-affiliated proliferation financiers, or fraudsters.

values.definition: Organised criminal groups laundering predicate-offence proceeds or running fraud through virtual assets.
State-linked actors conducting theft and laundering, such as DPRK-linked groups.
State-affiliated actors using virtual assets to finance weapons proliferation, such as DPRK-linked networks.
Individuals or groups conducting fraud, investment scams or address poisoning.
Actors using virtual assets to finance terrorism.

term_types.name: Intermediary role in illicit schemes
term_types.question: What role does an intermediary play in an illicit virtual asset scheme, serving one criminal network or several?
term_types.description: Classifies intermediaries by the part they play in illicit schemes, including whether they serve multiple criminal typologies at once.

values.definition: Intermediary serving one illicit typology, such as only fraud or only laundering.
Intermediary serving more than one illicit typology, such as both fraud and proliferation financing.
Virtual assets function both as the lure for fraud and as the channel for laundering proceeds.

term_types.name: Illicit laundering technique
term_types.question: Which method is used to obscure or move illicit virtual asset proceeds?
term_types.description: Classifies laundering techniques used to conceal the origin or movement of illicit virtual assets.

values.definition: Using unregistered or unlicensed VASPs to move proceeds.
Using mixing services to obscure transaction trails.
Moving assets across chains through bridges to break traceability.
Exchanging cash for virtual assets through swap networks.
Splitting or pooling funds across large wallet clusters.
Moving stablecoins such as USDT over low-cost networks such as Tron to evade tracing.

term_types.name: Reason for illicit virtual asset use
term_types.question: Why do criminals prefer virtual assets for the illicit activity?
term_types.description: Identifies the attributes that make virtual assets attractive for illicit use, such as anonymity, speed or stability.

values.definition: Obscuring identity of parties to transactions.
Rapid cross-border movement of value.
Stable value attractive for holding or moving proceeds.
Low transaction cost and ready liquidity.
Spreading funds across assets to reduce detection risk.

term_types.name: Fraud and scam scheme type
term_types.question: What kind of fraud or scam is being perpetrated with virtual assets?
term_types.description: Classifies fraud and scam schemes involving virtual assets by their mechanism.

values.definition: Long-running fake investment scams that gradually extract funds from victims.
Sending small transfers from look-alike addresses to trick victims into copying them.
Scams using AI-generated content such as deepfakes or synthetic identities.
Fraud or laundering conducted through online gambling services.

term_types.name: AML and sanctions-evasion risk factor
term_types.question: Does the feature amplify money laundering, terrorist financing, or sanctions-evasion risk?
term_types.description: Identifies features of crypto-assets or activities that increase ML/TF or sanctions-evasion exposure.

values.definition: AI-enabled crime such as deepfake scams or AI-assisted exploit development.
Asset design that prevents lawful freezing, blocking or burning of units.
Peer-to-peer transfers via unhosted wallets with limited visibility and no obliged reporting entity.
Services provided into a jurisdiction from outside its legal territory, subject to weak or absent licensing.
Dormant or non-trading VASP deposits and withdrawals used for layering.
Typologies arising from weak or uneven FATF standard implementation, notably by VASPs in weakly supervised jurisdictions.
Shared infrastructure such as stablecoins, OTC brokers, RPC nodes or bridges used across multiple illicit schemes.

term_types.name: Linked financial crime threat
term_types.question: Which related financial crime threat is linked to the illicit virtual asset activity?
term_types.description: Identifies financial crime threats, such as proliferation financing, terrorist financing or sanctions evasion, that co-occur with virtual asset misuse.

values.definition: Financing of weapons of mass destruction proliferation.
Provision of funds for terrorist activity.
Circumvention of targeted financial sanctions.

term_types.name: Offshore VASP home regime strength
term_types.question: Is the offshore VASP's home regulatory framework strong or weak, and is it licensed by host jurisdictions?
term_types.description: Assesses offshore VASPs by the strength of their home regulatory framework and host-jurisdiction licensing requirements.

values.definition: Home jurisdiction has a strong regulatory framework for the VASP.
Home jurisdiction lacks a strong framework, and host licensing is absent or weak.

term_types.name: Offshore active service to jurisdiction
term_types.question: Does the offshore entity actively serve customers in a jurisdiction, or maintain material local substance?
term_types.description: Determines whether an offshore VASP actively targets customers in a jurisdiction regardless of physical presence, and whether it has local substance such as a compliance officer.

values.definition: Solicits or serves customers in the jurisdiction, regardless of physical presence.
Does not actively serve customers in the jurisdiction and lacks material local substance.

term_types.name: VASP licensing or registration status
term_types.question: Where is the VASP incorporated or licensed, and is it already a licensed financial institution?
term_types.description: Classifies VASPs by place of incorporation, business location, and whether they are already licensed financial institutions.

values.definition: Incorporated or registered in the jurisdiction with a licence or registration.
Incorporated abroad or providing service into the jurisdiction from offshore.
Already licensed as a financial institution with full FATF obligations, and so exempt from separate VASP treatment.

term_types.name: VASP exemption from separate treatment
term_types.question: Is the entity already an existing financial institution exempt from separate VASP treatment?
term_types.description: Separates existing financial institutions with full FATF obligations from entities subject to separate VASP treatment.

values.definition: Already licensed with full FATF obligations and so exempt from separate VASP treatment.
Subject to separate VASP licensing or registration.

term_types.name: Money transmitter status
term_types.question: Does the person accept and transmit value for others, or perform a non-transmitter function?
term_types.description: Determines whether a person is a money transmitter, user, or exempt supplier based on function and purpose.

values.definition: Accepts and transmits value or CVC for others.
Anonymises or transacts only for its own purposes, not for others.
Supplies tools such as communications, hardware or anonymising software as trade.

term_types.name: Anonymising service type
term_types.question: Does the provider offer anonymising services such as mixing, or only supply anonymising software?
term_types.description: Separates providers of anonymising services, which are money transmitters, from providers of anonymising software, which are not.

values.definition: Mixes or tumbles CVC for others and is classed as a money transmitter.
Supplies anonymising software without transmitting value for others, and is not a money transmitter.

term_types.name: Integral activity exemption status
term_types.question: Is the business distinct from money transmission, or is transmission necessary to its operation so the exemption fails?
term_types.description: Applies the integral exemption, which excludes businesses whose operation is distinct from and does not require money transmission.

values.definition: Business is distinct from money transmission and transmission is not necessary for its operation.
Transmission is necessary for or integral to the business, so the exemption does not apply.

term_types.name: Mining activity status
term_types.question: Does the miner use mined CVC only for itself, or transmit value for others?
term_types.description: Classifies CVC miners and pool operators by whether their activity amounts to money transmission.

values.definition: Uses mined CVC solely to buy goods or services for itself and is not an MSB.
Uses mined CVC to transmit value for others and is an MSB.
Distributes earned CVC to members as integral to authentication services and is not money transmission.

term_types.name: Payment processor exemption status
term_types.question: Does the CVC payment processor meet the exemption conditions?
term_types.description: Determines whether a payment processor qualifies for exemption based on facilitation through BSA-regulated clearance systems.

values.definition: Facilitates purchases through BSA-regulated clearance systems and meets exemption conditions.
Does not meet the payment processor exemption conditions.

term_types.name: Anonymity-enhanced provider type
term_types.question: Is the anonymity-enhanced CVC provider centralised or decentralised, and does it receive or transmit value?
term_types.description: Classifies anonymity-enhanced CVC providers by payment system type and by value receipt or transmission.

values.definition: Centralised anonymity-enhanced payment system that receives or transmits CVC for others.
Decentralised anonymity-enhanced system where the provider does not receive or transmit CVC for others.

term_types.name: Hosted wallet provider role
term_types.question: Is the hosted wallet owner a user, an agent of the host, or a financial institution?
term_types.description: Classifies the role of a hosted wallet owner, which determines due diligence duties.

values.definition: Wallet owner acting for itself and not as an agent of the host.
Wallet owner acting as agent of the hosted wallet provider.
Wallet owner or host is a domestic or foreign financial institution.

term_types.name: Supervisory authority type
term_types.question: Is the supervisor a competent authority or a self-regulatory body?
term_types.description: Separates government competent authorities from self-regulatory bodies in supervising VASPs.

values.definition: Government authority responsible for supervising VASPs.
Non-government body supervising its members under delegated powers.

term_types.name: Federal regulator mandate
term_types.question: Which market or institution type does the regulator supervise?
term_types.description: Sorts U.S. regulators by the market or institution type under their mandate.

values.definition: Regulator of securities markets such as the SEC.
Regulator of commodity and derivatives markets such as the CFTC.
Industry self-regulatory body such as FINRA or the NFA.
Banking regulator supervising specified types of depository institutions.

term_types.name: Regulatory scope entity category
term_types.question: Which category of entity falls within the regulation's scope?
term_types.description: Identifies which entity types are covered by a regulation's scope provisions.

values.definition: Performs one or more listed crypto-asset services under MiCAR.
Holds funds linked to credit agreements, excluding those acting under a creditor's responsibility.
Provides listed trust or company services.
Provides gambling services involving the wagering of stakes.
Provides crowdfunding services through matching of funders and projects.
Holding company whose subsidiaries are financial or non-financial in composition.

term_types.name: DORA financial entity category
term_types.question: Under which regulated financial entity category is the entity authorised?
term_types.description: Classifies entities by the sectoral regulatory category under which they are authorised.

values.definition: Authorised as a credit institution.
Authorised as an investment firm.
Authorised as a payment or e-money institution.
Authorised as a central counterparty or trade repository.
Authorised as a fund manager or insurance or intermediary undertaking.
